Convert a PK/PD mrgsolve model into a `sim_tte_ode()`-ready model

Source: R/tte_model.R
tte_model.Rd

Writes the survival scaffold (p11, U, END, the TEVT/event_found/T_PRE/P_PRE/P_POST in-solver event-detection latch – sim_tte_ode's own mechanism) onto a user's own mrgsolve PK/PD model, exactly the mechanical edit list every shipped *_hazard.cpp library model already documents by hand at the top of its [PROB] block – generalized here to any model with an $ODE/$DES block, not just the six shipped backbones. See vignette("bring-your-own-model", package = "simtte") for the full mechanics (block-locating/splicing, the name-collision policy) and worked examples.

Usage

tte_model(model, hazard, params = list(), name = NULL, bsv_targets = NULL)

Arguments

model

One of: a file path to a model file; a character vector of model code (either one string with embedded newlines, or already one line per element – both accepted); or a compiled mrgmod (its own source is read back from mod@code). Must declare an $ODE or $DES block – a $PKMODEL/$PRED-only model is rejected, since the survival compartment has to be co-integrated in the same ODE system; use the ODE-form equivalent from modlib instead (e.g. "pk2cmt", not "pk2"). A simtte_model (this function's own return class) is rejected – convert the original model again with a different hazard/params instead of converting an already-converted one.

hazard

Character scalar: one C++ expression for the instantaneous hazard HAZ, written in terms of any name already in scope inside the model's own $ODE/$DES (states, $GLOBAL #defines, $MAIN locals, $PARAM values) plus whatever names params adds – e.g. "H0 * exp(lp + beta_cp * CP)". Include lp in the expression if sim_tte_ode's covariates/ beta mechanism should affect this model; lp is always declared (default 0) whether or not the expression uses it.

params

Named list, the hazard's own parameters and their population-default values (e.g. list(H0 = 0.01, beta_cp = 0)). Must not name lp, U, or END – those three are always added automatically (defaults 0, 0, 1e9, matching every shipped *_hazard.cpp model) and are rejected if present here.

name

Character scalar or NULL (default): passed to mcode_cache as the model name (caching and print() only). Left at NULL, a name is derived from an MD5 hash of the converted code, so two different conversions never share a build directory/model name even if called back to back – mcode_cache() is normally content-hash aware under a repeated name (verified, verified directly), but two builds under the same name landing in the same filesystem-timestamp second can defeat its underlying make-based rebuild check (verified directly – exactly the pattern an automated test loop hits, converting many small variants back to back); hashing the default name sidesteps this rather than relying on mcode_cache()'s own detection. A caller-supplied name does not get this treatment (it is used verbatim, for predictable caching across sessions) – avoid reusing one name for genuinely different hazard/ params content called in quick succession.

bsv_targets

Character vector or NULL (default): the parameter names sim_tte_ode's omega argument may target via its per-subject-idata route. Ignored (with a message()) if model already declares its own $OMEGA block – that model already has a working BSV route (omat), and the two never combine for the same model.

The compiled model is built into simtte_model_cache (never a global mrgsolve option). Using the result in a separate process (a cluster worker, a chunked/array job task – see ?sim_tte_ode "Parallel simulation"): pass this object to simtte_prepare_model there; it rebuilds from $code automatically if the compiled object this function returned does not resolve in that process (its shared object lives wherever this process's own cache put it), so correctness never depends on the two processes sharing a filesystem.

Value

An object of class "simtte_model", a list with code (the converted model source, printable directly with cat(x$code, sep = "\n")), mod (the compiled mrgmod), hazard, hazard_params (the fully resolved parameter list, including the always-added lp/ U/END), bsv_targets, name, and source (how model was supplied: "code", "file", or "mrgmod"). Pass the whole object as sim_tte_ode's model argument.

Details

Call this first, then pass the result to sim_tte_ode as its model argument. In a parallel or multi-process run, run the result through simtte_prepare_model on each worker.

Nothing in the input model is edited in place except its $GLOBAL/$MAIN blocks (both singleton in mrgsolve; every other addition – a new $PARAM, $INIT, an $ODE block carrying only the hazard link, a $CAPTURE block – is appended as a brand-new block at the end of the file, never spliced into the model's own $ODE/$DES content.

See also

sim_tte_ode, which takes this function's return value as its model argument and runs the simulation. sim_tte_ode_models, if a built-in model already fits and no conversion is needed. simtte_prepare_model, to make the converted model usable in another R process; simtte_model_cache shows where it is compiled.

Examples

# \donttest{
# mrgsolve::modlib() itself needs mrgsolve *attached* (library(mrgsolve)),
# not just installed; mrgsolve::mread() with an explicit 'project' reaches
# the same internal model library without that requirement.
irm1 <- mrgsolve::mread(model = "irm1",
  project = system.file("models", package = "mrgsolve"), compile = FALSE)
tm <- tte_model(irm1,
  hazard = "H0 * exp(lp + beta_r * (RESP / (KIN / KOUT) - 1.0))",
  params = list(H0 = 0.01, beta_r = 0),
  bsv_targets = c("CL", "V2", "KIN", "KOUT"))
#> Building simtte_tte_model_0f9e7be42471 ... 
#> done.
tm
#> <simtte_model> "simtte_tte_model_0f9e7be42471" (source: mrgmod)
#>  hazard: HAZ = H0 * exp(lp + beta_r * (RESP / (KIN / KOUT) - 1.0)) 
#>  parameters:
#>    H0 = 0.01 
#>    beta_r = 0 
#>    lp = 0 
#>    U = 0 
#>    END = 1e+09 
#>  between-subject variability: via idata, targets: CL, V2, KIN, KOUT 
#>  $code: 98 lines -- cat(x$code, sep = "\n") to view
sim <- sim_tte_ode(model = tm, n = 20, end = 30, delta = 5, seed = 1)
head(sim$events)
#>   ID  sim_time sim_status     sim_reason
#> 1  1 30.000000          0 administrative
#> 2  2 30.000000          0 administrative
#> 3  3 30.000000          0 administrative
#> 4  4  9.628203          1          event
#> 5  5 30.000000          0 administrative
#> 6  6 10.715139          1          event
# }
